summary: Make evidence-based CVA design and payment-oversight decisions. Explore the five-day course and review the curriculum.
lede: Cash and voucher assistance (CVA) design training helps humanitarian and social-protection teams assess markets and make evidence-based programme choices. Participants use EMMA evidence and the Minimum Expenditure Basket to compare modalities, document transfer-value assumptions and account for market constraints. They also map digital-payment risks, consider protection and access safeguards, and prepare feedback, monitoring and oversight plans that connect emergency transfers with social-protection systems.
audienceIntro: This intermediate course is designed for professionals who shape CVA programme choices or oversee the systems that deliver and monitor assistance. It suits humanitarian and social-protection teams working across programme, operations, MEAL, government and donor functions.
modules: CVA Decision Context and Programme Logic
prerequisites: Working familiarity with humanitarian response, social-protection programming or programme operations is expected. No coding is required; exercises focus on programme decisions, operational records and oversight artefacts.
